correctness.rationale: A rung fixes both vertices of its column; along a rung-free interval rail counts on the interfaces then alternate between zero and two, giving disjoint dimers. The only rung-free matchings are the two rim pairings, regular for even n and exceptional for odd n. For n≥4 a square is necessarily two neighboring rungs and the two connecting rails: zero rungs would require the whole rim, odd rung count would require at least n rails, and two rungs force the two connecting rails. Toggling one dimer gives the Lucas-cube edges, and deleting then inserting differing dimers realizes Hamming distance. The count is L_n plus the odd exceptions; for each possible dimer, its containing independent sets correspond to the F_(n−1) independent sets of the remaining path, giving nF_(n−1) edges. For odd n the symmetric difference with a regular matching contains an odd number of rungs. Numbering rim vertices modulo 2n, these rungs contribute n mod 2n, so the signed rim displacement needs at least n unit steps. A single such flip costs at least n+1, and flipping directly between the exceptions costs 2n. The unique rim-path matchings after removing both endpoints of one rung, together with that rung, give one alternating arc-plus-rung of length n+1 from either exception. The cutoff is inclusive. The analytic proof covers all n≥4; the frozen Python and C++ checks were read, not executed.
residual_risks: Hamming distance is a square-flip statement, not a claim about distances after all longer cycles are allowed.
